documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology follow-up, 8 weeks after laparoscopic left adrenalectomy.

No spells since surgery. Recovered well, back at full duty at the warehouse. Taking amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, atenolol, metformin and risperidone. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Healed port sites. Heart regular.

Pathology: pheochromocytoma 3.0 cm, confined to the gland, negative margins.

Results: plasma free metanephrine 39 and normetanephrine 92 pg/mL, both normal. Biochemical cure.

Plan:
1. Pheochromocytoma resected and biochemically cured.
2. All patients with pheochromocytoma are offered germline genetic testing; he agreed, sample sent today. We will send the result.
3. Yearly plasma metanephrines for surveillance.
4. Blood pressure management continues with primary care.

Endocrinology

documents.title: January labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.9 and kidney function and potassium normal. Endocrinology says your hormone levels are normal now after surgery - great news. Keep the same medicines and I'll see you in April with fasting labs first.

documents.title: Genetic testing result
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Germline multigene panel for hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma: no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant detected. Result reviewed with the patient by phone. Plan unchanged: plasma metanephrines yearly, next due January 2024.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: chest/breast size.

HPI: Here for his diabetes follow-up after the adrenal surgery and endocrinology visits, but the main thing he wants to talk about is his chest. Over roughly the last year both breasts have gotten bigger. He is embarrassed by it, won't take his shirt off at the beach or the pool anymore. Not painful. No nipple discharge. No medicine changes recently (risperidone since last May). Weight has gone up a lot since surgery.

Meds: risperidone 2 BID, metformin 1000 BID, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atenolol 50. NKDA.

Exam
Weight 100.6 kg, BMI 34. BP as charted.
Chest: breasts enlarged symmetrically. Skin normal, no retraction, nipples normal. Palpation: soft diffuse fatty tissue, I do not feel a firm or rubbery disc beneath either areola. No axillary nodes.
Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender, no edema.

Labs 4/7 (fasting): glucose 146, A1c 7.2. TC 220, HDL 35, LDL 145, TG 250. ACR 91.

A/P
1. Pseudogynecomastia - fatty enlargement with the weight gain, no glandular tissue or mass on exam. Reassured; the most effective step is weight loss. Talked through realistic goals, cutting soda and fast food on shifts, walking on days off.
2. Obesity, BMI now 34, up from 30 a year ago.
3. DM2 - A1c 7.2 on metformin 1000 BID. Continue.
4. HTN - continue.
5. CKD 1 - ACR 91, creatinine normal in January.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Annual update to primary care. Mr. Reyes remains on risperidone 2 mg twice daily. Stable mood and thought content, no psychotic symptoms, no hospitalizations, working full time. Informed of his adrenal surgery last fall; recovered well. Continue current dose; follow-up every 2-3 months.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated retinal exam 07/11/2023: no diabetic retinopathy OU, no macular edema. Corrected vision 20/20 each eye. See again in a year.

orders.reason: Persistent itching and peeling between toes despite OTC antifungals

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM/HTN follow-up.

Taking meds. Weight about flat since April. Psych stable.
New: feet have been itching and peeling between the toes for months. Has tried a couple of drugstore antifungal creams on and off, it calms down then comes right back. Wants it looked at properly given his diabetes.

BP 136/86. 
Feet: peeling and scaling in the web spaces between the toes on both feet. No open sores, no redness spreading onto the foot, no nail changes noted. Monofilament intact, pulses good.
Heart RRR, lungs clear.

A/P
- Toe-web peeling not clearing with OTC treatment in a diabetic: referral to dermatology. Keep feet dry, change socks midshift.
- DM2: A1c drawn today, BMP.
- HTN: 136/86, continue three agents.
RTC 3-4 months; flu shot when available.

documents.title: A1c
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your A1c is 7.4, a little higher than April. Kidney labs normal. Same plan - metformin twice a day and keep chipping away at the soda. Dermatology referral is in; they will call you.

documents.title: Flu vaccine outreach
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called to offer flu shot at a nurse visit. Pt declines this year, says he'll think about it. Will offer again at next visit.

medications.sig: Apply to the affected areas between the toes twice daily for 4 weeks

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology new patient visit

34-year-old man referred by primary care. History of schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes and obesity; recently evaluated by his PCP for pseudogynecomastia.

Several months of itching and peeling between his toes. It came on gradually and goes up and down despite over-the-counter creams. Worse when he wears his tight work shoes for long shifts; better on weekends when he is barefoot at home. At work he uses shared locker rooms and showers, and a few coworkers have had the same thing. No fever, joint pains or other systemic symptoms.

Medications: risperidone, metformin 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atenolol 50 mg. NKDA.

Exam: Both feet show peeling and scaling in the interdigital web spaces. No vesicles, no cellulitis. Remainder of the exposed skin is clear.

Procedure: scraping taken from the web spaces for KOH preparation and fungal culture.

Assessment: tinea pedis (interdigital), clinically.

Plan: ketoconazole 2% cream twice daily for 4 weeks to the web spaces, continuing a week past clearing. Dry thoroughly between toes, moisture-wicking socks, rotate work shoes, and wear sandals in the shared showers. We will send the KOH and culture results.

Dermatology

documents.title: Outside immunization: COVID-19 2023-2024
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Registry import: Pfizer-BioNTech 2023-2024 COVID vaccine 10/28/2023 at a pharmacy. Flu shot still declined per our outreach.

documents.title: Dermatology results
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body: Results from the 10/16 scraping of the toe web spaces: KOH preparation showed septate hyphae; fungal culture grew Trichophyton rubrum. This confirms tinea pedis. Continue the ketoconazole cream as directed. Return as needed.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his car on lunch break, consented to video format.

Feet are clear - used the ketoconazole for the full month, wears sandals in the work shower now. Derm results showed a common foot fungus.
A1c 7.1 last week, slightly better than August's 7.4. Kidney labs normal. Still on metformin twice a day, says he's had fewer sodas.
No spells, no headaches. Home BP cuff reads 130s/80s.
Psych stable on risperidone.

A/P
- Tinea pedis resolved.
- DM2: continue metformin.
- HTN: continue.
- Physical in March with fasting labs. Flu shot offered again, still declines.
